bug_description.original: A heap buffer overflow (out-of-bound read) occurs in cil_print_recursive_blockinherit in libsepol/cil when the CIL compiler encounters a recursive blockinherit with an optional block. This happens because cil_print_recursive_blockinherit() assumes that all nodes are either CIL_BLOCK or CIL_BLOCKINHERIT, leading to incorrect handling of other block kinds.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 39-byte ASCII witness `(block b2(optional o(blockinherit b2)))` is parsed into an AST where `blockinherit b2` sits under `optional o` inside the outer `block b2`. During `CIL_PASS_BLKIN_LINK`, `cil_resolve_blockinherit_link()` resolves the nested blockinherit's `block_str` back to the enclosing block `b2` and records that AST node in `b2->bi_nodes`; during `CIL_PASS_BLKIN_COPY`, `cil_resolve_blockinherit_copy()` detects the recursive inherit and calls `cil_print_recursive_blockinherit()`. That printer only distinguishes `CIL_BLOCK` from everything else. When its parent walk reaches the intermediate `CIL_OPTIONAL` node, it casts `curr->data` to `struct cil_blockinherit *` and evaluates `NODE(((struct cil_blockinherit *)curr->data)->block)`. On a `struct cil_optional`, the misread `block` field aliases `optional->datum.name`, which for this witness is the pooled 2-byte string `"o"`. `NODE(...)` then dereferences that 2-byte string as though it were a `struct cil_symtab_datum`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 at `libsepol/cil/src/cil_resolve_ast.c:2348`. The patch fixes the bug by handling `CIL_BLOCKINHERIT`, `CIL_OPTIONAL`, and other node flavors separately instead of blindly treating every non-block ancestor as a blockinherit.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled CIL symbols into parse-tree nodes backed by pooled heap strings.
source.value_from: The staged file `gt_results/arvo_28462/poc` is the exact 39-byte ASCII text `(block b2(optional o(blockinherit b2)))` with no line terminator. This statement interns each witness symbol into the string pool; the one-byte optional name `o` becomes the exact 2-byte heap allocation later read past at the ASan sink.

tainted_value_origin.description: For the witness `(optional o ...)` form, this picks the pooled string pointer `"o"` out of the parse tree. `cil_gen_node(..., CIL_OPTIONAL)` stores that same pointer in `optional->datum.name`, which the vulnerable printer later misreads as a `struct cil_block *`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `NODE(...)` dereferences the misread pointer value as a `struct cil_symtab_datum *`; on this path that pointer is actually the 2-byte pooled string `"o"`, so the dereference performs the reported 8-byte heap out-of-bounds read.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at this line and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 2-byte region allocated from `cil_parser.c:261` via `cil_strpool_add` / `cil_strdup`.

root_cause.description: Inside the recursive-blockinherit printer, every non-`CIL_BLOCK` ancestor is treated as though `curr->data` were a `struct cil_blockinherit`. When the ancestor is actually `CIL_OPTIONAL`, this cast reinterprets `optional->datum.name` as the `block` field of a blockinherit object.
root_cause.note: The patch inserts an explicit `curr->flavor == CIL_BLOCKINHERIT` branch and separate handling for `CIL_OPTIONAL` / other flavors, so optional nodes are logged without reading blockinherit-only fields.

parser_admitted.condition: For the staged witness `(block b2(optional o(blockinherit b2)))`, `cil_parser(name, buffer, size + 2, &db->parse)` returns `SEPOL_OK`, so `cil_add_file()` does not reject the input and compilation proceeds into AST building and resolution.

recursive_linked.condition: The witness resolves the nested `blockinherit b2` back to the outer `block b2`, so the blockinherit AST node is recorded in `b2->bi_nodes` and later revisited during `CIL_PASS_BLKIN_COPY`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness passes the 39-byte witness CIL text into `cil_add_file()`, which parses it and hands the resulting parse tree to AST construction.
AST construction turns the witness into an outer block `b2`, an inner optional `o`, and a nested `blockinherit b2`, preserving the parent chain `blockinherit -> optional -> block`.
Resolution links the nested blockinherit back to block `b2`, records it in `b2->bi_nodes`, and the later recursive-blockinherit printer miscasts the intermediate optional node as a blockinherit.

When the printer evaluates `NODE(((struct cil_blockinherit *)curr->data)->block)` on the optional ancestor, it dereferences the 2-byte string `"o"` as if it were a `cil_symtab_datum`, and ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8.

fine_trace.note: The parser interns each attacker-controlled symbol from `(block b2(optional o(blockinherit b2)))` into the string pool and stores the resulting pointer in a parse-tree node. For the witness token `o`, `cil_strpool_add()` allocates the 2-byte heap string that ASan later identifies as the over-read object.

fine_trace.code: key = parse_current->next->data; rc = cil_gen_node(db, ast_node, (struct cil_symtab_datum*)optional, (hashtab_key_t)key, CIL_SYM_BLOCKS, CIL_OPTIONAL);
fine_trace.note: When AST building reaches `(optional o ...)`, it selects the pooled string pointer `"o"` as `key` and inserts a `CIL_OPTIONAL` node. `cil_gen_node()` / `cil_symtab_insert()` store that same pointer in `optional->datum.name`, which is the field later misread as a block pointer.
For the nested `(blockinherit b2)` form, AST building stores the attacker-controlled target name pointer `"b2"` in the new `struct cil_blockinherit` object.

When the walk visits the witness's nested `blockinherit b2`, `ast_current` is the optional AST node from step 2, so the new blockinherit node becomes a child of that optional. The enclosing `block b2` remains one level higher, giving the later parent walk the chain `blockinherit -> optional -> block`.

fine_trace.code: inherit->block = (struct cil_block *)block_datum; if (inherit->block->bi_nodes == NULL) { cil_list_init(&inherit->block->bi_nodes, CIL_NODE); } cil_list_append(inherit->block->bi_nodes, CIL_NODE, current);
fine_trace.note: The BLKIN_LINK pass resolves `inherit->block_str` (`"b2"`) to the enclosing block datum, stores that block pointer in `inherit->block`, and appends the current blockinherit AST node to `b2->bi_nodes`. This both defines the recursion target used later in `block == bi->block` and makes the node reachable from the block-copy pass.
During BLKIN_COPY on the original block node `b2`, the resolver iterates `b2->bi_nodes` and invokes the recursive-check helper on the registered nested blockinherit node.

The recursive-check walk starts at `bi_node->parent`, skips the optional ancestor because `curr->flavor != CIL_BLOCK`, then reaches the enclosing `block b2`. That block's `struct cil_block *` equals `bi->block` from step 5, so the recursion predicate fires and the printer is called with `terminating_node = curr`.

fine_trace.code: if (curr != bi_node) { cil_list_prepend(trace, CIL_NODE, NODE(((struct cil_blockinherit *)curr->data)->block)); }
fine_trace.note: Root cause. In the printer's parent walk, the intermediate optional node is neither `CIL_BLOCK` nor `bi_node`, so the `else` arm assumes `curr->data` is a `struct cil_blockinherit`. On a `struct cil_optional`, reading `((struct cil_blockinherit *)curr->data)->block` fetches bytes at offset 8 of the optional object, which is really `optional->datum.name` and therefore the pointer to the 2-byte string `"o"`.

Sink. `NODE(...)` treats the fake `block` value from step 8 as a `struct cil_symtab_datum *` and dereferences its `nodes` field. Because that value is actually the 2-byte heap string `"o"` allocated from step 1, the dereference performs the saved 8-byte read exactly at the start of that 2-byte allocation, producing the ASan heap-buffer-overflow report.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer trace says the faulting 2-byte heap region was allocated from `cil_parser.c:261` via `cil_strpool_add()` and `cil_strdup()` while interning the witness token `o`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch rewrites `cil_print_recursive_blockinherit()` so only `CIL_BLOCKINHERIT` nodes are cast to `struct cil_blockinherit`, while `CIL_OPTIONAL` and other flavors are logged without dereferencing blockinherit-only fields.

poc.trigger: The staged 39-byte ASCII file is passed by `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` into `cil_add_file(db, "fuzz", data, size)`. Parsing and compilation of that single CIL buffer reach recursive blockinherit handling and crash before policy emission.

format.name: CIL source text
format.contract: Exactly the staged 39-byte ASCII witness `(block b2(optional o(blockinherit b2)))` with no trailing newline. The verified trigger is limited to this layout: one outer block named `b2`, one optional named `o` nested directly inside that block, and one nested `blockinherit b2` inside the optional, so the parent chain from the blockinherit node to the terminating block contains a `CIL_OPTIONAL` node between the recursive `CIL_BLOCKINHERIT` and the enclosing `CIL_BLOCK`. This contract does not generalize beyond that witness.
